title: Profit Center × Equipment-Centric
summary: Service is a margin line earned on a contracted installed base. Margin is won or lost on three things: enforcing what the contract covers, billing everything else, and fixing the machine on the first visit.

tiers.label: Tier 1: Go-live
tiers.description: Without these, service cannot be run as a margin line.

tiers.label: Tier 2: Phase two
tiers.description: Builds margin and capacity once the core loop is stable.

tiers.label: Tier 3: Later or optional
tiers.description: Worth doing when the data from Tiers 1 and 2 is trustworthy.

jobs.title: Enforce contract entitlements at dispatch
jobs.detail: Check coverage, response commitment, and covered parts when the request is logged, so billable and covered work are split before anyone rolls a truck.

jobs.title: Tie every work order to a serialized asset
jobs.detail: No asset, no work order. This is what makes entitlement, warranty, and history possible later.

jobs.title: Schedule and dispatch by skill, territory, and response commitment
jobs.detail: The board shows which jobs are at risk of breaching the contract, not just who is free.

jobs.title: Put asset history in the technician's hands before arrival
jobs.detail: Prior faults, parts replaced, open cases, and the covering contract on the mobile work order.

jobs.title: Capture parts consumption on the work order
jobs.detail: Every part used is recorded against the job and decremented from van stock, so it is either covered or billed.

jobs.title: Price billable work from the contract and price list
jobs.detail: Labor and parts pricing come from the agreement and the price list, not from technician judgment.

jobs.title: Invoice within an agreed number of days of job completion
jobs.detail: Completion triggers billing review automatically. The number of days is a target the client sets in discovery.

jobs.title: Generate planned maintenance from agreement schedules
jobs.detail: PM visits are created from the contract, not remembered by the branch.

jobs.title: Replenish and transfer van stock
jobs.detail: Truck stock levels drive replenishment, and transfers between technicians are tracked.

jobs.title: Recover supplier warranty on failed components
jobs.detail: Claims against suppliers are raised from the work order instead of a separate tool.

jobs.title: Report service margin by branch and service line
jobs.detail: One view, filtered per branch, built on the blueprint KPIs.

jobs.title: Quote repairs and contract renewals from the field
jobs.detail: Technicians flag and quote out-of-contract work and lapsed coverage while on site.

jobs.title: Offer customer self-service for requests and asset status
jobs.detail: Customers log requests against their own assets and see job status without calling the branch.

jobs.title: Create cases from connected-equipment alerts
jobs.detail: Machine telemetry opens a case before the customer notices a fault. A step toward the Servitization row.

kpis.name: First-time fix rate
kpis.definition: Share of jobs resolved on the first visit with no return trip for the same fault.
kpis.whyItMatters: Every return trip is unbilled labor on a contract job and a hit to the customer's uptime. It is the clearest test of whether parts and history reach the technician.
kpis.whatGoodLooksLike: Rising quarter over quarter, with repeat visits traced to a named cause (part, history, or skill).

kpis.name: Contract attach rate
kpis.definition: Share of installed units sold or in service that are covered by an active service agreement.
kpis.whyItMatters: The installed base only earns recurring margin if it is under contract. This is the growth lever for a profit-center service line.
kpis.whatGoodLooksLike: Rising, with renewals tracked and lapsed units visible to sales and to technicians on site.

kpis.name: Service gross margin
kpis.definition: Service revenue less the direct cost of labor, parts, and travel, as a share of service revenue.
kpis.whyItMatters: This is the number service leadership is asking to be judged on. The other KPIs explain why it moves.
kpis.whatGoodLooksLike: Reported by branch and service line from the system, not assembled in a spreadsheet.

kpis.name: Entitlement leakage
kpis.definition: Work performed free that the contract did not cover, plus covered work that was billed in error.
kpis.whyItMatters: Leakage in either direction costs margin or customer trust. It is the direct measure of whether entitlement checks work.
kpis.whatGoodLooksLike: Trending toward zero, with every override logged and attributable.

kpis.name: Unbilled completed work
kpis.definition: Value of completed jobs that have not yet been invoiced, including parts consumed but not billed.
kpis.whyItMatters: Meridian's parts and invoicing pain shows up here first. It is cash the business has earned and not collected.
kpis.whatGoodLooksLike: Small and aging quickly, with no job completed without its parts recorded.

kpis.name: Days from completion to invoice
kpis.definition: Elapsed time between a job being marked complete and the invoice being issued.
kpis.whyItMatters: Slow invoicing delays cash and invites disputes because the visit is no longer fresh for the customer.
kpis.whatGoodLooksLike: Falling toward the target the client sets in discovery, and consistent across branches.

kpis.name: Mean time to repair
kpis.definition: Average elapsed time from a fault being reported to the asset being back in service.
kpis.whyItMatters: It is what the customer experiences and what response commitments in the contract are written against.
kpis.whatGoodLooksLike: Falling, and reported against each contract's response commitment rather than as one average.

kpis.name: Technician utilization
kpis.definition: Share of paid technician hours spent on productive work orders rather than travel, waiting, or admin.
kpis.whyItMatters: Labor is the largest cost in the service margin. Better routing and less paperwork show up here.
kpis.whatGoodLooksLike: Rising without first-time fix falling, which would signal rushed work.

questionSet.question: Walk me through what happens from the moment a customer calls with a down machine to the moment a job exists.
questionSet.whyWeAsk: It shows who touches the request, what gets captured, and whether the asset and contract are identified up front.
questionSet.goodAnswer: The agent identifies the customer and the serial number, sees the contract, and creates the job with coverage already known.

redFlags.answer: "The branch takes it from there."
redFlags.signals: Intake varies by branch. Expect a different version of the process in every branch.

redFlags.answer: "We usually figure out the machine when the tech gets there."
redFlags.signals: No asset on the job, so entitlement and history cannot work at dispatch.

questionSet.question: How does the person taking the call know what this customer's contract covers?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: Entitlement enforcement is a Tier 1 job. We need to know where the contract terms live today.
questionSet.goodAnswer: Contract terms such as covered parts, labor, and response time are on the customer record and visible at intake.

redFlags.answer: "They look it up in the warranty tool, or ask the branch manager."
redFlags.signals: Terms live outside the service system. Watch for an integration request later.

redFlags.answer: "The good ones just know."
redFlags.signals: Entitlement lives in people's heads, which means leakage is almost certain.

questionSet.question: When work is done that the contract does not cover, what happens?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: It tests whether billable work is caught or given away, and who has authority to decide.
questionSet.goodAnswer: The job is flagged billable at intake or on site, the customer approves, and it is priced from the price list.

redFlags.answer: "We usually eat it for good customers."
redFlags.signals: Unmanaged goodwill. Expect a request to skip entitlement checks for key accounts.

redFlags.answer: "The tech decides on site."
redFlags.signals: Pricing authority sits with technicians. Margin varies by who shows up.

questionSet.question: How does a dispatcher decide which technician gets which job?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: It reveals whether skills, territory, and contract response commitments drive dispatch or habit does.
questionSet.goodAnswer: Skills, location, and the contract's response commitment drive the choice, and the dispatcher can see who is at risk of breaching.

redFlags.answer: "Our dispatchers know the techs."
redFlags.signals: Dispatch knowledge is tribal. Expect resistance to a standard board.

redFlags.answer: "Whoever is closest."
redFlags.signals: Contract response commitments are not part of dispatch. Breaches are likely invisible.

questionSet.question: How are planned maintenance visits created today?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: PM on contract is recurring margin. We need to know whether it is generated or remembered.
questionSet.goodAnswer: PM visits are created from the agreement schedule, and missed PMs are reported.

redFlags.answer: "Each branch keeps a spreadsheet."
redFlags.signals: PM delivery depends on the branch. Contract value is at risk of not being delivered.

questionSet.question: What does the dispatch board need to show that it does not show today?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: It separates real information needs from a request to rebuild the current screen.
questionSet.goodAnswer: The answer is framed as information, such as jobs at risk, parts status, and skills, rather than as a screen layout.

redFlags.answer: "Just make it look like the old one."
redFlags.signals: Likely off-blueprint request. Ask why before it becomes a Customization.

questionSet.question: When a technician uses a part from the truck, how does anyone know?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: Parts pulled off-truck without billing is a named Meridian pain point. This finds where the record breaks.
questionSet.goodAnswer: The part is recorded on the work order at the time of use and van stock is decremented.

redFlags.answer: "We reconcile at the end of the month."
redFlags.signals: Parts are invisible to billing. Unbilled completed work is likely high.

redFlags.answer: "Techs fill out a sheet when they restock."
redFlags.signals: Consumption is recorded after the fact and detached from the job.

questionSet.question: How often does a technician arrive without the part the job needs?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: Missing parts are a leading cause of low first-time fix in equipment-centric service.
questionSet.goodAnswer: It is tracked, and likely parts are suggested from the asset's fault history before dispatch.

redFlags.answer: "We don't really track that."
redFlags.signals: First-time fix cannot be explained yet. Baseline measurement is a Tier 1 need.

questionSet.question: Who owns van stock levels, and how are they replenished?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: It decides whether replenishment belongs in Tier 2 and who the process owner is.
questionSet.goodAnswer: A named role owns stock levels per van, and replenishment is driven by recorded consumption.

redFlags.answer: "Each tech manages their own truck."
redFlags.signals: No inventory accountability. Stock accuracy will need a clean-up before go-live.

questionSet.question: What does a technician know about the machine before they arrive?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: Missing asset history is the second named cause of Meridian's low first-time fix.
questionSet.goodAnswer: Prior faults, parts replaced, open cases, and the covering contract are on the mobile work order.

redFlags.answer: "They call the last tech who worked on it."
redFlags.signals: History lives with people, so it leaves when they do.

questionSet.question: What does a technician have to record before a job can be closed?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: Completion rules decide whether billing and history get clean data.
questionSet.goodAnswer: Labor, parts, resolution code, and customer sign-off are required to complete.

redFlags.answer: "They can close it and fill in the details later."
redFlags.signals: Data quality depends on goodwill. Invoicing will lag and history will be thin.

questionSet.question: When a technician spots out-of-contract work or a lapsed contract on site, what happens?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: In a profit-center cell, the technician is also a sales channel.
questionSet.goodAnswer: The technician can flag or quote it on the spot, and it reaches sales or the branch as a lead.

redFlags.answer: "That's not their job."
redFlags.signals: Revenue on the installed base is left on the table. Tier 2 sell-from-field may need change management.

questionSet.question: How long after a job is complete does the customer get an invoice, and what happens in between?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: Slow invoicing is a named pain point. The steps in between are where the delay lives.
questionSet.goodAnswer: Completion triggers a billing review with pricing already applied, and the invoice goes out within a set target.

redFlags.answer: "Paperwork comes back from the branch at the end of the week."
redFlags.signals: Batch, paper-driven close. Days from completion to invoice is likely long and variable.

redFlags.answer: "Billing re-keys it into the ERP."
redFlags.signals: Manual re-entry between systems. Expect an integration scope question.

questionSet.question: Who sets the price on billable service work, and where do they get it?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: Pricing from the contract and price list is a Tier 1 job. Exceptions here become Modifications.
questionSet.goodAnswer: Prices come from the agreement and the price list; discounts need approval.

redFlags.answer: "Each tech has their own rates."
redFlags.signals: Likely request for custom pricing per technician. Ask what business rule it really serves.

questionSet.question: How do you see service margin by branch today?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: It shows whether the margin-line ambition can be measured and who assembles the numbers.
questionSet.goodAnswer: One report, filtered by branch, built from system data.

redFlags.answer: "Each branch manager has their own spreadsheet."
redFlags.signals: Expect a request for a bespoke report per branch. One filtered view is the blueprint answer.

questionSet.question: Where is the list of every unit you have installed, and how accurate is it?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: The installed base is the foundation of this cell. Its data quality sets the migration effort.
questionSet.goodAnswer: One installed-base list with serial numbers, locations, and owners, maintained when units move.

redFlags.answer: "Between the ERP, the warranty tool, and the branches, we could piece it together."
redFlags.signals: The installed base needs consolidation before go-live. Plan data work, not just configuration.

questionSet.question: When a unit moves to a new site or a new owner, how does service find out?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: Stale asset records break dispatch, entitlement, and contract renewals.
questionSet.goodAnswer: There is a defined trigger, from sales or the technician, that updates the asset record.

redFlags.answer: "When the tech shows up at the old address."
redFlags.signals: No asset lifecycle process. Asset-history updates must be part of work-order close.

questionSet.question: Which machines generate the most repeat visits, and how do you know?
questionSet.whyWeAsk: It tests whether fault history is usable for first-time fix and for product feedback.
questionSet.goodAnswer: Resolution codes are captured consistently, so repeat faults can be reported by model.

redFlags.answer: "Everyone knows which ones."
redFlags.signals: No structured fault data. Resolution codes need to be defined early.

process.label: Aligned to vendor standard process catalogs.
process.note: Platform-agnostic. Each step lists the control the blueprint puts in place.

steps.name: Request
steps.description: Customer, portal, or alert raises a service request.

steps.name: Entitlement check
steps.description: Coverage, response commitment, and covered parts confirmed.
steps.guardrail: Billable versus covered decided before scheduling.

steps.name: Schedule
steps.description: Job booked against skills, territory, and the response commitment.
steps.guardrail: At-risk jobs visible on the board.

steps.name: Dispatch
steps.description: Work order sent to the technician's mobile device.
steps.guardrail: Asset history and likely parts attached.

steps.name: Execute
steps.description: Technician diagnoses and repairs on site.

steps.name: Parts
steps.description: Parts used are recorded against the job.
steps.guardrail: Van stock decremented at the time of use.

steps.name: Complete
steps.description: Labor, parts, resolution code, and sign-off captured.
steps.guardrail: Job cannot close with missing data.

steps.name: Invoice
steps.description: Billable work priced from contract and price list and invoiced.

steps.name: Asset-history update
steps.description: Fault, fix, and parts written back to the asset record.
steps.guardrail: Next technician starts with the full history.
